tagline: Two notches, and a stone face that is no longer there.
intro: From North Woodstock the trail runs north on US 3 into Franconia Notch, where the parkway between Cannon Mountain and Mount Lafayette keeps to one lane each way by a special act of Congress. At Twin Mountain it turns east onto US 302, passes Bretton Woods and follows the Saco River down through Crawford Notch to Bartlett and Glen, then south through North Conway. At Conway the Kancamagus carries the loop back to Lincoln, about 100 miles around.
Travelers came early. A turnpike went through Crawford Notch in 1803, and the Crawford family cut trails and kept inns there through the century that followed.

moments.title: Old Man of the Mountain
moments.text: Five granite ledges 1,200 feet above Profile Lake made a face in profile, first written down in 1805. It fell on May 3, 2003, and stays on the license plates.

moments.title: Mount Washington Cog Railway
moments.text: Up the base road from Bretton Woods, the first mountain-climbing cog railway climbs at 2.8 miles an hour on a charter one legislator said might as well reach the moon.

moments.title: Crawford Notch
moments.text: In August 1826 a slide came down the notch and buried the Willey family, who had fled their house for a prepared shelter. The house was untouched.

practical: The Bear Notch Road branch between Bartlett and the Kancamagus is open from spring to late fall and closed all winter.
